title: Fakhruddin Valika
wikitext:
{{Short description|Pakistani industrialist (died 1973)}}

'''Fakhruddin Valibhai Valika''' (died 1973) was a Pakistani [[industrialist]] who led the Valika Group, which had subsidiaries such as [[Naya Nazimabad|Valika Cement]], Valika Steel now known as Peoples Steel,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine|title=Private interest|first=Hussain Ahmad|last=Siddiqui|website=The News International}}</ref> Valika Chemicals, Valika Textile, and [[Muhammadi Steamship Company Limited]] until the [[nationalisation in Pakistan|nationalisation]] of major industries in Pakistan.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.geo.tv/latest/432738-the-rise-and-fall-of-karachis-valika-family-part-1|title=Rise and fall of Karachi's Valika family (Part 1)|website=Geo.tv}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.geo.tv/latest/433929-a-bombing-fall-of-dhaka-and-nationalisation-rise-and-fall-of-karachis-valika-family-part-2|title=A bombing, fall of Dhaka and nationalisation: Rise and fall of Karachi's Valika family (Part 2)|website=Geo.tv}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://pakobserver.net/family-business-in-pakistani-iv-valika-fancy-and-ispahani-by-ikram-sehgal/ | title=Family business in Pakistani-IV Valika, Fancy and Ispahani | by Ikram Sehgal | date=30 September 2022 }}</ref>

Fakhruddin Valika was born into a business family in Bombay, part of [[Dawoodi Bohra]] community.<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1152902 | jstor=1152902 | last1=Papanek | first1=Hanna | title=Pakistan's Big Businessmen: Muslim Separatism, Entrepreneurship, and Partial Modernization | journal=Economic Development and Cultural Change | date=1972 | volume=21 | issue=1 | pages=1–32 | doi=10.1086/450605 | url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Career==
In 1947, Valika setup the first [[textile mill]] of Pakistan near [[Metroville]], Karachi. It was inaugurated by [[Muhammad Ali Jinnah]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1351915 | title=70 years on: Looking back at key economic events in Pakistan's history | date=16 August 2017 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |title=Before and After Independence |last=Ahmad |first=Mushtaq |year=1989 |pages=214 |publisher=Royal Book Company |isbn=978-969-407-099-5 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=KDpuAAAAMAAJ&q=Fakhruddin+Valika}}</ref>

In 1959, Valika founded the United Insurance Company of Pakistan which was later listed on the [[Karachi Stock Exchange]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.theunitedinsurance.com/history-of-the-united-insurance-co/ | title=History of the United Insurance Co | date=19 November 2018 }}</ref>

In 1972, Valika Cement, Valika Chemicals, Valika Steel, and later [[Muhammadi Steamship Company Limited]] were nationalised with compensation. After the nationalisation of Valika Group companies, Fakhruddin Valika was arrested by the [[First Zulfikar Ali Bhutto government|Bhutto government]] and the event was shown live on the [[television]].<ref>{{Cite book |title=Law, State and Inequality in Pakistan |last=Azeem |first=Muhammad |year=2017 |pages=111 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-981-10-3845-7 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=t-AqDwAAQBAJ&dq=Fakhruddin+Valika&pg=PA111}}</ref>

Valika was a founding member of the [[Karachi Stock Exchange]].<ref name="auto">{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1973/01/01/archives/fakhruddin-v-valika-dies.html|title=Fakhruddin V. Valika Dies, A Pakistani Industrialist|work=The New York Times |date=January 1, 1973|via=NYTimes.com}}</ref> He was one of the patrons of [[cricket]] and [[field hockey]] in Pakistan.<ref name="auto"/> He also established several charitable organizations.<ref name="auto"/>
